notes: Treat accepted rows as already credited by the first manual SAIR submission.
The one-row 24T25000|r=4 submission was reported accepted by the user after this ledger was created.
The 24-row follow-up submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier, but scores were pending when recorded; it added no new pair keys and mostly collapsed to generic 24T25000.
Row 6 of that follow-up is a lower exact-nfdisc 24T25000|r=4 alternate, but it is not promoted as the representative until scoring confirms an improvement.
The 3-row strong anti-S24 follow-up was accepted by the SAIR verifier; it added new pair 24T21844|r=4 and two score-pending 24T24970|r=4 alternates.
Use this ledger for local queue planning only; official status remains the SAIR verifier/leaderboard.
The six-row r8_quartic_lift submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier; it added four r=8 pair keys: 24T657|r=8, 24T661|r=8, 24T1310|r=8, and 24T9993|r=8. Scores were pending when recorded.

The eight table rows from the r16_quadratic_lift submission were accepted by the SAIR verifier; all collapsed to 24T24979|r=16. The pair is absent from the frozen baseline. The SAIR CSV export marks scoreable=false only while scoringStatus=pending and scoringReason=discriminant_pending; field discriminants, score, solvability, and teams/k were still pending when recorded.

The 10-row diversified r16 probe submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier; exact-composed rows landed as 24T24979|r=16 and odd-perturbed rows landed as 24T25000|r=16. Both pairs are absent from the frozen baseline; scores were pending when recorded.

The 12-row anti-collapse r16 probe submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier; all rows landed as duplicate 24T25000|r=16 alternates. Multi-off-block divisor-2 perturbations did not escape the 24T25000 r16 basin, so future r16 work should require a genuinely different construction.

The 8-row r24 high-real-root probe submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier; all rows landed as duplicate 24T25000|r=24 alternates. The local r24 construction and SAIR formatting worked, but the low-odd perturbation family is generic-label collapsed, so future high-real-root work should pivot to r20 or a genuinely more structure-preserving anti-generic r24 family.

The 10-row r20 high-real-root probe submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier; all rows landed as duplicate 24T25000|r=20 alternates. The local r20 construction and SAIR formatting worked, but the low-odd mixed quadratic perturbation family is generic-label collapsed, so future high-real-root work should preserve more algebraic structure rather than widening this perturbation style.

The 10-row r12 exact-composed structured probe submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier; it added 24T22770|r=12, 24T24970|r=12, and 24T24979|r=12. Exact g(x^2) support avoided 24T25000, while 24T24979 was the dominant accepted basin. Scores were pending when recorded.

The 10-row r12 feedback-aware exact-composed follow-up submission was accepted by the SAIR verifier; rows 1-2 landed as 24T24970|r=12 and rows 3-10 landed as 24T24979|r=12. It added no new pair keys, but preserved useful score-pending alternates and confirmed exact g(x^2) still avoids 24T25000. Further nearby g(x^2) widening is lower priority; pivot to a different exact-composed/tower construction.
